numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Float and mixed int/float input passed with dtype="timedelta64[s]" to pd.Series (and DataFrame/pd.array) is interpreted as nanoseconds and then cast down to the coarser unit, silently truncating values to zero (e.g. pd.Series([1.5, 2.5, 90.0], dtype="timedelta64[s]") gives all 0 days; pd.Series([1, 2.5, 90], dtype="timedelta64[s]") gives all 0 days).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Numeric input, including float and mixed int/float input (and input with None/NaN/NaT/pd.NA), should be interpreted in the dtype's unit, matching to_timedelta(..., unit=...). E.g. pd.Series([1.5, 2.5, 90.0], dtype="timedelta64[s]") should hold 90 seconds for the last value rather than 0 days; integer input [1, 2, 3] already gives 1s/2s/3s.
trigger_conditions: dtype is timedelta64 with an explicit unit such as "timedelta64[s]"
input is mixed int and float (e.g. [1, 2.5, 90])
input contains missing values (None/NaN/NaT/pd.NA) in numeric data
constructed via Series, DataFrame, or pd.array
